findings.text: Readahead expansion is available to other memory management code to grow an existing readahead window to cover a newly requested range in both directions.

Readahead expansion requires the current start to already be aligned to the mapping minimum folio size and keeps all growth quantized to that minimum while aligning each insertion index to mapping requirements.

Readahead expansion stops without further growth when a page cache entry is already present at the frontier or when folio allocation or insertion fails, and trailing growth also extends synchronous and asynchronous readahead sizes when caller state is present.
During readahead expansion the first encounter of a working set folio latches a working set flag and enters memory stall accounting exactly once for the operation.
Anonymous VMA preparation ensures a VMA has an associated anonymous VMA, reusing a neighbour when possible and otherwise allocating a new root, then publishing it to the VMA.

Anonymous VMA preparation requires the mmap lock held for writing and may sleep, then takes the anonymous VMA write lock before the page table spinlock while publishing, releasing them in reverse order.
A newly allocated anonymous VMA starts with a self parent count and gains an active VMA count only when successfully attached, with unused chain or VMA objects released after unlock.
Mergeable anonymous VMA lookup checks the successor VMA before the predecessor VMA to find a reusable anonymous VMA for the current VMA.
An anonymous VMA is reusable only when the two VMAs are compatible and the donor VMA has exactly one chain entry, with the donor pointer read once under pairing with release publication.
Anonymous VMA compatibility needs adjacency, equal memory policy, same file, equivalent flags ignoring access and merge ignored bits, contiguous file offsets and contiguous anonymous offsets.
Two dedicated slab caches hold anonymous VMA objects and anonymous VMA chain links for the reverse mapping subsystem.

Boot initialization creates the anonymous VMA and chain slab caches with accounting and panic on failure, using safe reclamation for the VMA cache and a constructor that initializes locking, zero reference count and empty tree.
Anonymous VMA constructor initializes the per object read write semaphore to unlocked state so later readers and writers can coordinate reverse map walks and modifications.
Dirty aware unmap flush checks the current task batch state and performs a pending TLB flush only when a writable entry was recorded.
Flushed shift equals sixteen, pending mask equals thirty two thousand seven hundred sixty seven, and large pending threshold equals sixteen thousand three hundred eighty three.

Pending TLB flush recording ignores inaccessible entries, otherwise records architecture pending range, marks flush required, orders batch flag after PTE clear, increments a per address space batched counter with reset under contention when pending grows large, and latches writable on dirty.
Deferral of TLB flush is allowed only when batching was requested and the architecture permits deferral, while the alternate build never defers and treats pending recording as a no operation.

Per task unmap batch moves from idle to pending once a mappable entry is recorded, latches writable on first dirty entry, and returns to idle after an explicit flush, with a separate per address space pending count that is periodically reset to avoid overlap with flushed count.
Referenced scan argument aggregates remaining map count, referenced result, accumulated VMA flags and an optional memory cgroup used for filtering.

Per VMA referenced check walks all mappings of a folio, restores missed locking when fully mapped under one page table, skips unshared swap backed pages of exiting tasks, batches large folio checks, clears young state through generation look around or direct flush, and stops early when all mappings are accounted.
Referenced and cleaning walks skip VMAs without recency or from a different cgroup during targeted reclaim, and cleaning walks additionally skip all non shared VMAs.

Folio referenced query returns zero when unmapped or without mapping, attempts opportunistic folio lock when caller did not lock, performs a try locked reverse map walk accumulating flags, and reports contended walks distinctly from referenced counts.

Page cleaning helper write protects and cleans dirty or writable present entries at both small and huge page granularity under notifier protection, flushing caches before clearing and reinstalling entries as clean and read only.
File write protect state carries a cleaned counter plus file offset, starting frame number and page count that define the range to be cleaned in each VMA.

Mapping wide write protection walks file mappings over a given range and returns total cleaned pages, treating a missing mapping as zero work, while the single VMA variant resolves the address from file offset and skips non shared VMAs.

Unmap batch sizing limits work to one page for poisoned, small, swap backed anonymous or unused entries, otherwise groups entries bounded by one virtual area and one table level while respecting original writability and soft dirty state.

Poisoned huge page unmap handles one mapping for each virtual area under notifier protection, unshares middle tables for file pages under try lock, flushes caches, clears the huge entry, propagates dirtiness, installs a poison swap entry, updates usage counts and drops reverse map and reference.

Lazy free anonymous reclamation orders page table clear before reference count sampling, reconverts to swap backed on redirty unless droppable, rejects pages with extra references beyond mapping count, and decrements anonymous usage on success.
Swap entry preparation preserves exclusivity, soft dirty indication and user fault fd state from either a present entry or a device exclusive entry when building the replacement swap entry.

Anonymous VMA preparation can fail with out of memory when chain or VMA allocation fails, readahead expansion can stop early leaving a partially grown window, and pending TLB counter reset uses compare exchange retry to avoid overflow overlap.

Lock restoration is skipped when table crossing is detected during missed lock handling, unexpected huge page mappings trigger a one time warning, and poisoned huge unmap assumes poison flag plus poison operation and a present entry matching the folio.
This translation unit enables trace point creation for its reverse mapping trace events.
Anonymous VMA initialization, folio referenced query, mapping range write protection, frame range cleaning and dirty aware unmap flush are provided for use outside their defining files.
